app.Response.description: The Response struct is used for wrapping the API response with a code, message, and data.

code.description:
Code is the HTTP status code or a custom code used to indicate the result of the request
@example 200

data.description:
Data is the response data (can be any object or null)
@example {"id": 1, "name": "John Doe"}

msg.description:
Msg is the message that describes the result of the request
@example "Request successful"

author_id_str.description:
AuthorIDStr is the same uid as a string. TikTok uids exceed 2^53, so JavaScript consumers of the numeric
author_id receive a rounded value; read this field instead. author_id stays for existing typed clients.

address.example: 304 Ord St, Los Angeles, CA 90012, USA

info.description: Crawlora is a hosted web-data and SERP API: call documented REST endpoints and get normalized JSON instead of HTML to parse — across search/SERP, maps and local, e-commerce, app stores, social, media and finance. One API key; Crawlora runs the proxy rotation, headless browsers and parsing behind the scenes. Billed pay-on-success: charged only on a successful 2xx response, 1-10 credits per call, with a free tier of 2,000 credits per month and no card. A hosted MCP server (mcp.crawlora.net/mcp) exposes the same catalog as agent tools. Search endpoints accept `q` as a universal alias for whichever search-term parameter they document (`query`, `term`, `keyword`, or Amazon's `k`), so one parameter name works across the whole catalog; an explicitly supplied documented name always wins.
info.title: Crawlora API

get.description: Calls the app's cached-pull feed route - `GET /tiktok/feed/offline/v2` - which answers protobuf, and returns a schema-free decode: field numbers become keys, printable length-delimited fields become strings and nested messages become objects, plus a flat list of every string leaf (`strings`), which is the fastest way to mine video ids and captions. Field numbering is inferred because TikTok publishes no schema for this message. This is the cached/offline pull variant, not the primary `POST /aweme/v2/feed/` feed already exposed as `/tiktok/mobile/feed/post`. The route is signature-validated, so it needs device-backed request signing to be configured for the deployment and fails with an error when it is not.

parameters.name: pull_type

parameters.name: count

get.description: Calls the app's primary feed route - `POST /aweme/v2/feed/`, which the Android client sends with a protobuf request body and answers with protobuf - and returns a schema-free decode: field numbers become keys, length-delimited fields become strings when printable, nested messages when they parse and base64 otherwise, plus a flat list of every string leaf. Field numbering is inferred because TikTok publishes no schema for this message; use the JSON `GET /tiktok/mobile/feed` route when you need the stable structured contract.

get.description: Returns the reference set the app's "go LIVE" flow uses to tag a stream: the general LIVE hashtags (`hashtags`, measured 18 entries of `{id, image, namespace, title}`, where `id` 0 is the "None" tag), the live-studio/live-voice/third-party hashtag subsets (`live_studio_hashtags` 16, `live_voice_hashtags` 16, `third_party_hashtags` 9), the single `game_hashtag`, and a 1,500-entry game catalogue (`game_tag_list`, `game_tag_count`) where every entry carries the same 12 keys: `id`, `short_name`, `show_name`, `full_name`, `bundle_id`, `package_name`, `game_category` (`[{game_type, title}]` with PC games/Mobile games/Console games/Others), `hashtag_id`, `hashtag_list`, `gar`, `landscape` (0/1/2) and `is_new_game`. The upstream is `/webcast/room/hashtag/list/` on the webcast edge host (no origin header); the measured body is 539,361 B and byte-identical on both working webcast hosts, `language`/`count` do not change it, and there is no cursor/has_more, so it is a one-shot reference dump. Measured 2026-10-22 with the pure-Go (device-free) signer, so it does not need the device-backed signer.

get.description: Returns one LIVE room's detail, keyed by `room_id` — the numeric id that `/api/v1/tiktok/mobile/live/search` returns under `data[].lives.author.room_id`. The upstream is `/webcast/room/info/` on the webcast edge host (no origin header), captured from the running 47.4.3 app's LIVE surface and reproduced against the live gateway. The response projects the fields callers key on — `title`, `status` (2 = live), `user_count` (concurrent viewers), `create_time`, `owner` (user id, nickname, avatar), `stats` (cumulative `enter_count`/`total_user`, `watch_user_count`, `like_count`, `comment_count`, `share_count`, `follow_count`, `replay_viewers`), `stream` (playable `flv_pull_url` per resolution plus `default_resolution`/`candidate_resolution` and the HLS/RTMP URLs) and `cover` — and keeps the upstream room object unmodified in `data` (it has ~500 keys, so a partial struct would drop fields). Measured 2026-10-22 with the pure-Go (device-free) signer: one room returned 193-198 KB with 1,595-1,600 concurrent viewers, 27,916 cumulative viewers, 27,096 enters and FLV URLs for FULL_HD1/HD1/SD1/SD2. `anchor_id` is deliberately NOT forwarded: it was measured to suppress the audience-only `stats.total_user` (27,916 -> 0 on the same room). A missing, non-numeric or unknown room id answers the webcast envelope's status 10011 and is surfaced as a 400; a finished room (status 30003) is a 400 too. The route is not signature-gated, so it does not need the device-backed signer.

parameters.description: Numeric LIVE room id from /api/v1/tiktok/mobile/live/search (data[].lives.author.room_id)
parameters.name: room_id

400.description: Invalid input, an unknown/not-live room, or a finished room

get.summary: LIVE room detail: status, viewers, owner, stream URLs, cover

get.description: Returns the LIVE room a TikTok user is currently streaming, keyed by `user_id`. The upstream is `/webcast/room/info_by_user/` on the webcast edge host (no origin header) and returns the same room payload as `/api/v1/tiktok/mobile/live/room` (title, status, concurrent viewers, owner, cumulative stats, per-resolution FLV URLs, cover and the ~500-key room object in `data`), except that the caller addresses a user and the room id is filled from the payload (both `user_id` and `room_id` are echoed). Measured 2026-10-22 with the pure-Go (device-free) signer: `user_id=6707748031095751686` answered 184,575 B (195,220 B on the second webcast host); `anchor_id` alone answers a 57-byte empty payload, so `user_id` is the address. A user with no live room answers status 30003 "room has finished" and is surfaced as a 400; a non-numeric user id is a 400 (status 10011); a bare call answers a 57-byte empty success envelope, which is why this endpoint requires `user_id`. The route is not signature-gated, so it does not need the device-backed signer.

parameters.description: Numeric TikTok user id (e.g. the owner id from a profile, video author or live search row)
parameters.name: user_id

400.description: Invalid input, or the user has no live room right now

Unlike the feed, this route PAGES for real: `count` is honoured (measured 1 -> 1 item with `cursor: 1, has_more: 1`; 5 -> 5 items with `cursor: 5`; 10/100 -> all 8 collections) and `cursor` advances (measured `count=5&cursor=5` -> the remaining 3 with `has_more: 0`). A negative count answers upstream status 5, which is rejected locally. Measured 2026-10-21 with the pure-Go (device-free) signer: 8 collections total. The route is not signature-gated, so it does not need the device-backed signer.

get.description: Returns one place's compact record, keyed by the `poi_id` that the place search endpoint returns. The upstream is TikTok's POI read (`/tiktok/poi/get/v1`), the record behind a place card: `name`, `address`, `category`, `average_price`, `latitude`/`longitude`, `city_code`/`region_code`, `review_score` with `review_count`/`no_rating`, `video_count`, `favorite_count`, `opening_hours`/`opening_status`, `cover`, `share_url`/`share_desc` and `parent_poi`, plus the upstream POI object unmodified in `place` so a richer field is never lost. This is the cheap lookup to use instead of the ~1 MB slash detail page when only the place record is needed. A nonexistent id answers 400 (the upstream business status 3009009 "poi not exist" is a caller error, not an outage). Measured 2026-10-21 with the pure-Go (device-free) signer: 4,594 B for a coffee shop (score 4.7 / 2 reviews, price "$", hours "8:00 AM – 5:00 PM", 11 videos), 4,623 B for a second location (score 4.8 / 13 reviews). get.description: Returns one place's photo album, keyed by the `poi_id` that the place search endpoint returns. The upstream is `/tiktok/poi/picture_album/v1`: `categories` holds each album tab (`name`, `pic_tab_typecode`, `pictures` of bare image URL lists and `pictures_v2`, the same photos with `author` attribution, `pic_id`, `source` and origin/compressed URL info), `photo_count` sums the categories' pictures, and `title` is the app's own header. Measured 2026-10-21 with the pure-Go (device-free) signer: one place answered 5,368 B, title "Gallery (3)", 1 category with 3 photos whose `pictures_v2` entries name the Google-places contributor; another answered 24,196 B with more photos. The album is one-shot: `count` and `pic_tab_typecode` were measured and did not change the page. A nonexistent id answers 500 (the upstream answers status 4 "Server is currently unavailable" on this route, unlike the poi-not-exist code the other place routes use). The route is not signature-gated, so it does not need the device-backed signer.

parameters.description: Place id from the place search endpoint
parameters.name: poi_id

get.description: Returns one video's own captions translated into the requested language, as TikTok's caption/language (`cla`) service serves them. The response carries the track twice: `webvtt` is the upstream WebVTT text verbatim, and `cues` is the same track parsed into `{start_ms, end_ms, start, end, text}` records so a caller does not have to implement WebVTT. `video_id` is the aweme id returned by the feed, search, profile-posts and hashtag endpoints. Measured 2026-10-21 with the pure-Go (device-free) signer: the Korean-caption video 7696141388324293918 answered 11 English cues for `language=en`, and the same video answered Japanese, Chinese, Spanish, French, German, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Arabic, Hindi, Indonesian, Thai, Vietnamese, Turkish and Italian tracks; a Portuguese-lyrics video answered an 18,494-character English track (240 cues). Track size is a snapshot rather than a contract (the upstream re-translates from a cache), so assert a non-empty track in the requested language, not a byte count. The route is not signature-gated, so it does not need the device-backed signer. A video with no captions answers 400 (upstream status 5); a nonexistent video answers 500 (upstream status 4).
